newsitem.title: USA: Yugo corn export forecast trimmed - U.S. attache.
newsitem.headline: Yugo corn export forecast trimmed - U.S. attache.

text.p: An agricultural attache revised Yugoslavia's corn production and exports for marketing year 1997/98 to 5.0 million tonnes, down 400,000 tonnes from last month's estimate, according to a report made public on Friday.

"According to trade sources, in MY 1995/96, Yugoslavia exported 270,000 tonnes of corn, which contrasts with our earlier estimate for MY 1995/96 of 500,000 tonnes," said the report prepared by the U.S. Embassy in Belgrade.
The corn was shipped mostly to Romania, Bulgaria, Macedonia, Russia and Slovenia.

"Because of the decrease in our production estimate as well as an overvalued domestic currency, Yugoslavia's MY 1996/97 corn exports are currently projected at 250,000 tonnes, down 7.5 percent from a year earlier and down sharply from our last projection of 1.0 million tonnes," the report said.
Trade sources said about 150,000 tonnes of corn were exported during October 1996-June 1997, the report said, in barter transactions for fuel and gas.

The report also reduced projections for Yugoslavia's wheat imports in marketing year 1996/97 from 300,000 tonnes to 270,000 tonnes."According to trade sources, Yugoslavia's traders finished their marketing year 1996/97 wheat imports by purchasing around 15,000 tonnes from Hungary in June," the report said.
Wheat production in marketing year 1997/98 was still estimated to be 2.5 million tonnes, up 40 percent from the previous year, the report said.
Yugoslavia includes the Republics of Serbia and Montenegro.
Agricultural attache reports are not considered official USDA data.
